questions.question: OP-01/O110 (AX-6, D168 asked again under this session's ground): an SFTP server on Linux serves /proc/self/status as an item, size 0 in its attributes at open; O1 streams it, nothing changes it. The ground read (specs 051 to 053, profile 052, shared.md, the catalogue) has no clause on a stream's length; D159 and D166 do. Which length does an SFTP stream stop at?

options.label: Size at open, as D168 (Recommended)
options.description: D168 stands: SFTP's length fixed at open is the size the server reports at open; a stream ends at the earlier of the end a read meets and that size; NP10's scope reads 'Local and SFTP streams'. The procfs file starts Exhausted and delivers nothing, as on Local: one rule on every backend (D159). D168's reason 'freeze-2 can follow the pull request that carries it' reads 'freeze-2 follows /observe-review's full re-run (RFC-0029 R2)'. Source: D159, D166; server side not run.

options.label: Read to the end met on SFTP
options.description: D159 and D168 amended for SFTP: the reported size is not used; a stream reads until a read meets the end, so the procfs file is delivered whole and NP10 stays Local-only. Bytes O3 appends under E4 may be delivered; the read after the last byte contacts the server and can fail (Failed); D158's 'starts Exhausted for an empty item' no longer holds on SFTP; D43 gains a variation row. Source: D159 option (b).

questions.question: OP-01/O109 (AX-6, gap in D168): an SFTP server reports an item's attributes without a size (no size flag; paramiko's st_size is None); O1 streams it. No length is fixed at open, so D158's entry into Exhausted, D159's 'earlier of the end it meets and the length' and NP10's 'at most that size' have nothing to work from. What does the stream do?

options.label: End a read meets (Recommended)
options.description: With no size reported, no length is fixed at open: the stream ends where a read meets the end and enters Exhausted when that read returns its end value; it starts Open even for an empty item; bytes O3 appends under E4 may be delivered; NP10 does not reach it. D43 gains a row 'Length at open': normal value known at open (D159), declared deviation unknown, ending where a read meets the end (an SFTP server that reports no size). Cost: the read after the last byte contacts the server and can fail (Failed), as D158's option (b). Source: D158 option (b); io.RawIOBase (0 bytes signals the end).

options.label: Fail at open
options.description: The stream's open fails with the base category (D33) when the server reports no size: no length is ever guessed, D158 and D159 hold unchanged on every stream that opens, but an item such a server serves cannot be streamed at all, though it is readable. D96's Stream open column gains the case. Source: unsourced.

OP-01/O111 (AX-15, close-out): D170's Length at open row declares 'unknown' for 'an SFTP server that reports no size', a fact of one item's reply, while D82 makes every declaration static per backend. What does SFTP declare, and how does a caller learn it?

options.label: SFTP declares unknown (Recommended)
options.description: Static per backend: the row's deviation reads '(SFTP)'. Every SFTP store declares unknown; a caller assumes the weaker value on every SFTP stream and learns it per store through OP-18 (D44). D170's per-stream behaviour is unchanged: a stream whose server reports a size meets the normal value, which the deviation admits, as strong admits eventual. D82 unchanged.

options.label: Per-item condition
options.description: D82 is amended to admit a declaration conditioned on the item's own attributes reply, not only the store's location. The row stays as written; a caller cannot learn from the store's profile which streams have a length.

options.label: Configuration selects
options.description: The SFTP store's configuration states whether its server reports sizes (D43's 'services that differ' clause); an unnamed server takes unknown. Adds a configuration key.

questions.question: OP-01/O112 (AX-10, close-out): a sysfs file has size 4096 at open and 23 bytes of content; Local or SFTP streams it, no E4. D166 and D168 end the stream cleanly at 23 bytes (NP10); D99 exempts from E12 only a short end 'because of E4'. Is a size at open an announcement under E12 on file-system backends?

options.label: Not an announcement (Recommended)
options.description: On Local and SFTP no transfer announces a length: POSIX read(2) returns 0 at the end, and paramiko 5.1.0 ends a read at the server's EOF status, never comparing st_size (source read). D99's sentence reads: a read that ends short of the size at open is never E12's, with or without E4; D26 and D48 govern under E4, D166 and D168 (NP10) otherwise. D166, D168, D170 unchanged.

options.label: Size is announced
options.description: A size at open is E12's announcement: the sysfs stream fails unavailable after 23 bytes except under E4. D166 and D168 are amended, NP10 removed, and procfs and sysfs files cannot be streamed.

questions.question: OP-01/O113 (AX-2, close-out): D155 adopts 'read1(n) with n < 0 returns 1 to r bytes ... none of these moves the position or the state', while D70 has every read draw from the one position and tell() return the bytes delivered. Which of D155's cases does 'none of these' cover?

options.label: Zero-size cases only (Recommended)
options.description: As io (BufferedReader.read1(-1) over 10 bytes returns 10, tell() then 10, run in O113): 'none of these' covers read1(0) and readinto1(b)/readinto(b) with len(b) = 0. read1(n) with n < 0 draws from the position as D70 says, tell() advancing by what it returns, and enters Exhausted when the bytes delivered reach the length (D158, D159). D155 amended only in that sentence.

options.label: n < 0 is a caller error
options.description: read1(n) with n < 0 raises as a caller error, so no case delivers bytes without moving. Departs from io and from D70's adopted BufferedIOBase contract; D155's option (a) amended.

PR #1209 review 5818518543, D171: on an SFTP server that reports sizes, a procfs file (size 0 at open, 1417 bytes) follows the normal value and delivers nothing. D171's deviation cell, now declared for every SFTP store, says 'ends where a read meets the end' (all 1417 bytes), so D171's 'which the deviation admits' is false, and per RFC-0030 C1 this blocks. Changing D171's cell is a disagreement with a close-out decision. Which route?

options.label: Reopen (D176 onward) (Recommended)
options.description: C2: an /observe reopen decides the Length at open deviation cell again, e.g. 'unknown: where the server reports no size at open, a stream ends where a read meets the end…; where it reports one, the normal value (SFTP)'. Then a full /observe-review (review 9) before freeze-2. About two more sessions. PR #1209 then either merges as 'not frozen' or carries the reopen.

options.label: C3 rewording only
options.description: Treat it as text: drop 'which the deviation admits' and reword D171's Decision and cell so they say both cases, with no new decision. Fast, and freeze-2 still follows the merge, but it rewrites what D171 decided without a dialog, which the reviewer flagged as the line C2 draws.

options.label: Route as a note
options.description: Keep D171 as it is; a D175-style routing sends the finding to the spec flow. Freeze-2 follows the merge, but this goes against the reviewer's C1 reading that a row a check runs on every SFTP store would state something false.
